# X of a Kind in a Deck of Cards.

@example Two piles of 3: the three 5s in one and the three 0s in the other.
[5,0,5,0,0,5]
=> true

@example Four 7s and six 3s. Piles of 4 can't take the six 3s, but piles of 2 work: two piles of 7s and three of 3s.
[7,7,7,7,3,3,3,3,3,3]
=> true

@example Two 2s and three 9s: no X of 2 or more divides both 2 and 3.
[2,2,9,9,9]
=> false

# A single card can't fill a pile of 2.
[4]
=> false

# Two equal cards: one pile of 2.
[8,8]
=> true

# One number seven times: a single pile of 7.
[6,6,6,6,6,6,6]
=> true

# A 0 seen only once spoils the deal, even though the 7s pair up.
[0,7,7]
=> false

# Every count is at least 2, but 4 and 9 have no common factor.
[2,1,2,2,1,2,2,1,2,2,1,2,2]
=> false

# Counts 3 and 6: piles of 2 don't work, but piles of 3 do.
[0,9,9,0,9,9,0,9,9]
=> true

# Counts 6, 10 and 15: every two of them share a factor, but no X
# divides all three.
[5,9999,0,5,9999,0,5,9999,0,5,9999,0,5,9999,0,5,9999,0,5,9999,5,9999,5,9999,5,9999,5,5,5,5,5]
=> false
